name: Jody Baker
life: “I first kept emergency bus money under the wrapper in a sewing kit.” People around Ferris Deli know Jody by a small Monday habit. Jody asks for the end slice and listens to the names the counter workers use for regulars.
voice: I thought the small pocket held a ring. It held bus money in case she wanted to leave.
appearance: Jody has a deep crease beside the mouth when smiling. Look for dark brown curls cut close behind the ears. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a sand-colored linen shirt with a folded shopping list secured by a miniature clip. In conversation Jody folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing.
personality: Likes beautiful, unnecessary things and gets cross with people who mistake poverty for a lack of taste. Jody takes longer choosing a cheap birthday card than an expensive coat.
agenda: To keep a little travel money in the dress for the next wearer.
family: Robin Kiln is Jody’s first cousin once removed. Jody chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. Robin brings a spare shopping bag. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The empty berth*, Robin says, “My scholarship covers lessons and nothing you wear to them.”
connections: Marco Fox. They preserve a pocket and a tie out of the same bolts of wedding cloth.

reactions.situation: The bride wants to keep the old pocket
reactions.response: Jody leaves the pocket in place while the bride tries the dress on.

reactions.response: Jody tells them which ordinary detail proved helpful on a previous occasion, then listens without suggesting an answer.
